description.narrative: The project aims to review and improve the design and application of the newly developed draft building code for health infrastructure in Ukraine, with focus on rehabilitation centers, using the support of Dutch knowledge and specialized expertise. The project has a positive impact on SDG 8: inclusive and sustainable economic growth through supporting productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation.

title.narrative: Increased impact of an existing PSD project

comment.narrative:
Project PCB24UA01: Healthcare Building Code rehabilitation that provides technical advice and support to the Ukrainian government and the members of the Working Group (WG) working on the development of the building code for rehabilitation centers in Ukraine.
It builds upon project MAG19UA01 that facilitates Dutch specialized expertise for the development of a set of recommendations to the state building norms of Ukraine(DBN B.2.2-10:2001 "Healthcare Facilities") that was submitted them to the Ukrainian government and were formally approved.
It also complements project PTM24UA01: study visit on rehabilitation centers from Ukraine to NL, complements and provides conceptual and technical input to project PCB24UA01.

comment.narrative: Ukrainian working group on rehabilitation centers

The project fits in the category of enabling environment for business development. The project proovides technical assitance to the the working group of the Ministry of Health (WG-MOH) supporting the development of the building code for rehabilitation centers. The following organizations are members of this group and actively acted as counterpart o the project: - The Ministry of Communities, Territories and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine MTU - The Ministry of Health (MOH): - The State Emergency Service - The institute for public health of the National Academy of Medical Sciences of Ukraine - Representatives of NGOs - Representatives of private sector (architectural and engineering company). Rehabilitation centers are at the core of the plans of the Ministries MOH and MTU of Ukraine as they are crucial for the short- and long-term economic recovery and the reconstruction of Ukraine in the context of the ongoing war. The project strengthens the technical quality of the State Building code of Ukraine in the chapter of rehabilitation centers. As result of this project, the regulatory framework for the building code for rehabilitation centers was improved. These legal framework provide the rules of the game to foster the involvement of private actors in the provision of rehabilitation services.

comment.narrative:
The project strengthens the technical quality of the State Building code of Ukraine in the chapter of rehabilitation centers; and provides expert advice to Ukrainian public and private stakeholders on its applicability and practical consequences of its implementation. As result of this project, the rules of the game are in place to enable and to leverage the involvement of private actors in the provision of rehabilitation services. Specifically for the private sector it facilitates market access for new companies providing rehabilitation services.
Three results were initially defined: i) inception Report, ii) report on Rehabilitation facilities; and iii) report on proposals for updated building code for rehabilitation facilities. During the inception phase adjustments were made regarding these results. The Ukrainian counterpart (Ministries and multistakeholder working group working on the health reform and the development of rehabilitation centers) requested a more hands-on approach by inviting OHC/EGM to comment and propose changes to draft documents prepared by them. In this way the support would be immediate beneficial to them which was important given the tight deadline they were working towards. The demand was to focus on rehabilitation centers for two vulnerable groups: children and adults (civilians and veterans of war).
Based on the requested changes the results/deliverables were reformulated into: 1. Inception Report 2. Advice on norms on rehabilitation care for children 3. Advice on norms on rehabilitation care for adults
